columns: Recall developing or emerging for awkward middle (5+4, 6+3, 7+2)

summative_rubric.title: Adding Machine — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: End-of-unit rubric covering all 5 expectations B2.1-B2.5. Used to score each child against four levels.

rows.expectation_text: use the properties of addition and subtraction, and the relationship between addition and subtraction, to solve problems and check calculations

levels.descriptor: Treats addition and subtraction as separate operations; cannot use addition to solve subtraction; does not recognise commutativity (4+3 vs 3+4 seen as different).
Recognises commutativity with prompting (after Lesson 1 swap demo); uses addition for subtraction occasionally with reminder.
Independently uses commutative property for addition; uses addition to solve subtraction (fact-family-recall); writes all four facts from a triangle.
Articulates the commutative property unprompted; flexes between addition and subtraction across all fact families; explains the special doubles case (3 facts only).

rows.expectation_text: recall and demonstrate addition facts for numbers up to 10, and related subtraction facts

levels.descriptor: Counts every fact from 1 on fingers; recall is essentially zero. Subtraction always done by counting back.
Fluent on +0, +1, +2 facts; finger-counts the rest. Subtraction by count-up or count-back; not yet by fact-family-recall.
Fluent (≤3 sec) on all addition facts to 10. Subtraction facts to 10 done via fact-family-recall (knows 6+3=9, so 9-3=6).
Fluent recall on facts to 10; can produce the swapped fact AND the related subtraction facts within 5 seconds. Beginning to extend to facts at 12-15.

rows.expectation_text: use mental math strategies, including estimation, to add and subtract whole numbers that add up to no more than 20, and explain the strategies used

levels.descriptor: Defaults to count-all on fingers for sums to 20. Does not yet name doubles, near-doubles, or make-ten as strategies.
Knows doubles 1+1 to 5+5; uses make-ten on the ten-frame with prompts. Cannot yet swap-then-make-ten for sums like 5+8.
Selects a strategy proactively, matches it to the fact (doubles for 6+6, make-ten for 8+5), AND verbalises the strategy steps in 1-2 sentences.
Auto-swaps for make-ten when the larger addend is on the right; volunteers alternative strategy combinations; uses estimation to predict whether a sum is reasonable.

rows.expectation_text: use objects, diagrams, and equations to represent, describe, and solve situations involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 50

levels.descriptor: Builds with counters but cannot draw a tape diagram or write an equation matching the story. Mixes up problem types.
Identifies problem type with prompting; draws a single-rectangle tape diagram with only the answer; writes correct equation.
Identifies all three problem types (change-add-to, change-take-from, part-part-whole); draws a tape diagram with both parts labeled; writes correct equation.
Recognises that the same tape diagram can represent multiple problem types; volunteers alternative equations; solves multi-step problems.

rows.expectation_text: represent and solve equal-group problems where the total number of items is no more than 10, including problems in which each group is a half, using tools and drawings

levels.descriptor: Distributes objects unevenly OR stops at 'fair share with leftover'; does not yet recognise that a leftover breaks the equal-group rule.
Shares evenly when totals divide cleanly; cuts leftover in half with prompting; sometimes drifts back to 'with leftover' answer.
Shares fairly between 2 or 4 sharers including the half-share case; writes the per-plate share with 'and a half' notation; explains why a half is needed.
Shares fluently with multiple half-cuts (e.g., 6÷4 = 1½ each); generalises the fair-share-with-half rule to other contexts (biscuits, fruit); volunteers when the share would need a quarter or third.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Apply this rubric to each child's combined evidence: diagnostic tracker (Lesson 1) + L2/L3/L4 formative trackers + summative worksheet (Lesson 5). The level achieved is the LOWEST of the relevant evidence sources for that expectation.

summative_task_script.title: Lesson 5 Summative Task — Equal Groups and Half Groups
summative_task_script.purpose: End-of-unit summative assessment. Captures evidence for B2.5 (equal-group sharing including halves) explicitly via the worksheet, with B2.4 reinforced through the modelling steps.
administration_steps: Bring children back to the carpet after the small-group rotations on Day 5.
Hold up the worksheet and walk through the three parts: (1) even-share scenes, (2) half-share scenes, (3) reasoning prompt.
Distribute one worksheet per child. Allow 15 minutes for completion.
Walk around and record per-child evidence on the equal-group tracker.
Collect worksheets and score against the rubric: 9-10/10 = Level 4; 7-8 = Level 3; 5-6 = Level 2; 0-4 = Level 1.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Part 1 (2 even-share scenes, score out of 4): captures B2.5 baseline. Part 2 (2 half-share scenes, score out of 4): captures B2.5 mastery (the half-cut move). Part 3 (reasoning prompt, score out of 2): captures the child's articulation of the fair-share-with-half rule. Total score out of 10. Map to summative rubric: 9-10 = Level 4 Exceeding; 7-8 = Level 3 Achieving; 5-6 = Level 2 Developing; 0-4 = Level 1 Beginning.

evidence_per_expectation.B2.1: Lesson 1 diagnostic — child produces swapped fact; Lesson 3 formative tracker — uses addition to solve subtraction.
evidence_per_expectation.B2.2: Lesson 1 diagnostic — recall fluency on facts to 10; Lesson 3 formative tracker — writes all 4 facts from a triangle.
evidence_per_expectation.B2.3: Lesson 2 formative tracker — selects, matches, and verbalises a mental strategy.
evidence_per_expectation.B2.4: Lesson 4 formative tracker — identifies problem type, draws tape diagram, writes correct equation. Reinforced by summative worksheet modelling.
